title: Query
description: The recommendation engine's input contract (RECOMMENDATION.md §1). Natural-language questions map to this by deterministic template, never by generation, so a question always resolves to the same query.

kind.description: 'marginal_value' answers 'what does my next $X buy?' via the budget frontier and its knees (DECISION.md §5) — usually the real question behind a stated budget.

target.description: A dimension (ordinal ranking), a metric (continuous), 'cost', or 'fit'.

ratio_to_frontier.description: Computed from continuous measurements only. Ordinal rubric scores can never produce a ratio (RECOMMENDATION.md §7).

horizon_months.description: Drives option value and expected decay (DECISION.md §6). A reader shipping in six weeks should weight substitutability near zero, and can.

decision_criterion.description: 'auto' derives from persona risk posture (DECISION.md §4) — this is where risk_tolerance finally does real work. Explicit values let a reader ask 'what if I'm willing to gamble?' and watch the answer change, which is itself informative.

constraints.description: Hard eliminations. Never softened into penalties (EVALUATION.md §4 rule 4).

preferences.description: QUERIES.md §8.3. Distinct from constraints: preferences re-rank, stay visible even when they lose, and get PRICED — 'this preference costs $X/month and buys you Y'.

evidence_floor.description: Exposed as a query parameter so the engine degrades honestly instead of padding answers with weak evidence.

reference_date.description: graph_at(date). Enables historical replay: running a past query against past evidence reproduces what the Atlas would have said then (RECOMMENDATION.md §11.10).
